analyst_view.overall: Early view: Bologna arrive on a four-game winning run under Palladino, with Orsolini back from injury but Miranda a doubt after going off at Parma. Venezia have become harder to beat since Davide Nicola replaced Stroppa in October and beat Udinese 2-1 in their last game before the break. This is a Friday night game, and neither side plays in Europe, so both should be at full strength apart from injuries.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Venezia score only about 0.8 a game at home but concede 1.8, while Bologna's away games have averaged 2.7 goals, so the number fits. Nicola's Venezia now make opponents work for every goal, which keeps me from leaning higher.

corners.text: The site expects 9.1 corners, and both sides' records land on that: Venezia's home games and Bologna's away games have each averaged about nine. Bologna's wide pairs will win some, and Venezia's wing-back Hainaut, who set up a goal against Udinese, gives them a source of corners too.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. I lean lower: Bologna's away games have averaged only about 2.6 cards, and Bologna themselves collect just over one a game on the road. Venezia's home matches are a little higher, but not enough to reach four.

shots.text: The site expects 26.1 shots. I lean slightly higher, because Venezia's home games have averaged about 30 shots, with opponents taking almost 17 a game in Venice. Bologna's in-form attack had 33 shots at Parma, although that was against ten men.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. I lean slightly higher: Venezia's home games have averaged over ten on target, and Venezia allow about six a game. Bologna's away shooting has been accurate, at five on target a game.
